headline: Nasdaq-100 weekend halt: Tail low after Friday's record probe was fully retraced, while a steep long end, triple-digit Brent and a third carrier group deploying toward Iran keep Stress elevated
body: Friday closed the Nasdaq-100 at 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00% and a record close, after probing an intraday record of 31,017.53 and then giving back roughly 210 points to finish near the session low of 30,737.07. That completed retracement is the last observable price path before CME equity-index futures halted at 21:00Z, and it is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that this framework treats as Tail evidence. Every hour of the published forecast window falls inside that halt, which does not end until the Sunday restart at 22:00Z, beyond this horizon. The session was driven by a soft September employment report: 29,000 jobs added against roughly 90,000 expected, unemployment up to 4.2% from 4.1% and average hourly earnings at 0.1% month over month against 3.4% inflation. Bond traders cut October rate-hike odds to about 16% from roughly 64% a week earlier, and technology led, with Nvidia up more than 2% toward a $5.72 trillion valuation and Tesla up about 4% on 486,532 third-quarter deliveries. The VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59%, with a session range of 15.30 to 16.24, so there is no observed volatility expansion to carry into the weekend. Against that calm equity-volatility reading, the Stress inputs remain substantial. The Federal Reserve H.15 release puts the 2-year at 4.78%, the 10-year at 5.24% and the 30-year at 5.61% as of 1 October, a high and steep long end that keeps the discount-rate channel live. Brent trades near $102.25 and WTI near $91.11. Crude transit through the Strait of Hormuz has recovered to roughly pre-war volumes, largely via overland pipelines and transponder-dark shuttle tankers, but refined-product flows remain near 677,000 barrels per day against about 3.6 million before the war. Over 1 and 2 October the United States began moving a third carrier strike group and roughly 9,000 additional personnel toward the region while Iran's proposed seven-point Hormuz roadmap was rejected, which sustains an unresolved escalation channel. Under this framework that escalation raises Stress and bears on Confidence; it does not raise Tail while there is no session in which a pathological path could develop. Confidence is 87 and eases through the window as Friday's evidence ages. The shared Finviz context file was not usable for this run: its collection status is partial and its collection time is roughly 84 hours old, well outside the 90-minute freshness window, so it was disregarded and the assessment rests on independently verified primary sources. Dominant mode is recorded as normal, describing an orderly two-way close followed by a halted market rather than any directional regime.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the back half of Friday's payroll session and the first eighteen hours of the weekend halt. Tail stood at 20 through the European morning, firmed to 24 into the 12:30Z payroll release and reached 25 and then 27 across the 13:30Z cash open as the index gapped higher and extended toward its intraday record, the only stretch of the window that produced an orange state. Once that advance stalled and price retraced roughly 210 points into a close near the session low, Tail fell back to 22 and held between 21 and 23 through the U.S. afternoon. After the 21:00Z futures halt it dropped to 14 and then decayed steadily to 5 by the 10:00Z hour as the absence of a tradeable session removed the mean-reversion-failure mechanism. Stress fell from 79 at the cash open to 57 by the end of the window as volatility decayed, and dominant mode moved from trend-up during the opening extension to mixed and then normal once the halt began. Confidence stayed between 82 and 89 throughout. All 24 slots are backed by published Claude assessments and are reproduced here without hindsight revision.
outlookSummary: All 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME weekend halt: index futures closed on Friday at 21:00Z and do not restart until 22:00Z on Sunday, beyond this horizon. With no tradeable session there is no mechanism for sustained mean-reversion failure, so Tail is projected to hold between 3 and 4 and every hour maps to EA_ON and green. Stress eases from 55 to 50, remaining in the elevated band throughout, as Friday's volatility decay and recovered Hormuz crude transit are offset by a high and steep Treasury long end, triple-digit Brent, constrained refined-product flows and a third U.S. carrier group deploying toward Iran. Confidence declines gently from 87 to 80 to reflect Friday's closing evidence ageing across a weekend in which no new price path can be observed, and an unusable shared Finviz context file. Hour-specific notes mark the Friday session analogues, the weekend announcement window and the ageing of the evidence base; the nearest scheduled checkpoints, Monday's ISM Services PMI at 14:00Z and Wednesday's FOMC Minutes at 18:00Z, sit outside this window and are carried in the event calendar.
